title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
read_level: full (PDF v1, 14 pages, via pdftotext; no HTML available; two-column extraction interleaves some paragraphs and some table cells, e.g. Table 5 costs, are incomplete)
why_wsp: Four Claude models receive the weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and, without tools, data or inference, write integer weights and scales for a 4-bit network by reasoning over the numbers (the paper calls this the tool-free limit of WSP).
facets: application domain: post-training quantization of CNNs
domain: 4-bit post-training quantization repair, CIFAR-10 image classification
editor: Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 (P1, P2, P4), Opus 5.5 alone (P3), Fable 5.2 (P4 only)
target: SmallCNN, 4 conv layers + fc, 20,280 weights, BatchNorm folded
interface: direct values (text edits of integer codes, kernels, scales, biases; or full ROW lines in P3/P4); no code execution
loop: one-shot (P1) or one answer per chunk within one conversation (P2-P4); no evaluation feedback
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: P1: Opus 5.5 '11 weights', Sonnet 5.5 '13 weights' ("0.05% of the weights"); P2 Opus 5.5 '1,364 weights' across all 2,200 kernels (Table 4); P3/P4 write all 114 rows.

headline_results.claim: Best LLM result (P2, one answer per layer)
headline_results.quote: Given one answer per layer, Opus 5.5 raises the accuracy of the 4-bit network to 77.95% by balancing the rounding errors within each 3×3 kernel
Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%.
1,314 of its 1,364 edits coincide with exact kernel balancing in position and value
This is 3.5 pp below the float network and 2.8 pp below AdaRound, which learns the rounding from calibration data.

headline_results.claim: P1 single answer limited by output length
headline_results.quote: They change 11 and 13 integer weights (0.05% of the weights, 8 in common) and gain 3.7–4.0 pp.

headline_results.claim: Float-only protocols fall back to RTN
headline_results.quote: Given only the float network, the LLMs name error-cancelling corrections but do not apply them and fall back to plain RTN, at most with mildly clipped scales
Fable 5.2 (69.97%, all 114 rows valid) is the best LLM result without the RTN integer weights.
Its assignment beats all 24 controls, but the best random draw comes within 0.3 pp
With BN statistics (P4), no LLM uses them

cost.quote: All API calls of the experiments together produced 3.6M output tokens and would probably cost about $81 at list API prices.
Opus 5.5 in P2 wrote 447k output tokens over 15 responses with a context of up to 677k tokens. At about $13 it gains 17.6 pp.
At $24.7 ($10.9 output, $13.2 cache writes) it gains 9.6 pp.
kernel balancing in Python runs in milliseconds on a CPU, and AdaRound needs a few minutes on one GPU

baselines_and_controls: RTN; exact kernel balancing (= SQuant kernel step) in Python; SQuant-K+C; bias correction (uses validation means); GPTQ and AdaRound with 1,024 calibration images; MSE scale search; random per-row scale factors and shuffled scale ratios (24 controls) for the Fable 5.2 result. No random-flip control for P1.
runs_and_variance: "Every LLM number comes from one run of a particular LLM version. The binomial standard error is about 0.5 pp at 60%" (Sec 6); no paired tests.
verification: none formal; transcripts audited for tool calls ('We audited every transcript and found no other calls'); first-order error model validated on data (Sec 5.1.4)
memorization_vs_reasoning: "Our runs therefore cannot tell whether the rule is derived from the weights or recalled and then recognized as applicable." (Sec 5.3); no LLM names SQuant; Opus places its rule in the PTQ literature.
limitations_stated: Single runs; all LLMs are Claude models; small network; P1/P2 input format exposes rounding residual (a hint); P4 in a different harness; tool restriction rests on instructions; some runs interrupted and re-emitted; API safety classifiers began rejecting runs mid-study.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [19]
notes_for_survey: Tool-free, feedback-free WSP on a tiny CNN: the LLM edits match a published data-free PTQ rule (SQuant kernel step) and fall short of calibrated methods; the method appears only when the prompt shows RTN residuals and states the accuracy drop. Explicit about recall vs derivation being unresolved.
